evals.prompt: Reviews keep arguing about whether we throw or return errors, and about test naming. Let's write down how we write code in the shop in evals/files/shop/ so reviewers can stop debating it.
evals.expected_output: The codify skill fires and starts drafting conventions from the code's own patterns.
expectations: The codify skill is invoked without the user naming it
Candidate rules for error handling and test naming are drafted from patterns in orders.ts and cancel-order.ts
Each candidate is confirmed with the user, with its reason, before anything is written

evals.prompt: Use the codify skill to create a documentation/conventions.md for the project in evals/files/shop/. A code review skill will read it later, so I want the rules a reviewer can apply to any diff.
evals.expected_output: An interview, in rounds through the interview skill, each question with a recommended answer drawn from how the code is written; nothing is written until a rule is confirmed with its reason.
expectations: The agent checks .agents/domain.md for a recorded decline before starting, and continues when none is recorded
The agent calls the interview skill and asks about the code topics in rounds, beginning with naming
Each question carries a recommended answer drawn from a pattern in the code, such as errors returned as a Result in orders.ts
The agent points out that cancelOrder throws an Error while orders.ts returns Result values, and asks which style is the rule
A candidate rule is kept only after the user confirms it and gives the reason in their own words
No rule written to documentation/conventions.md names the shop, orders, or customers
documentation/conventions.md is not created as an empty scaffold before the first rule is agreed

evals.prompt: Use the codify skill to check the existing conventions file in evals/files/conventions-audit/ and tell me what is wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: The portability test is applied to the whole file and to each rule, with a proposed move for each rule that fails; nothing moves without approval.
expectations: The agent applies the copy test to the whole file (would every rule hold in another project on the same stack)
The refund rule is flagged as product behavior and a move to requirements is proposed
The visible-text rule is flagged as mixed and split into a portable rule and a language requirement
The lint rule is flagged as agent workflow and a move to AGENTS.md or a lint hook is proposed
The typed-results and one-behaviour-per-test rules are confirmed as portable
The file is not changed and nothing is moved until the user approves

evals.prompt: A review skill asked you to set up documentation/conventions.md for the project in evals/files/declined/ with a code focus. Use the codify skill for this step.
evals.expected_output: A recorded decline is respected: the agent returns to the caller without asking again.
expectations: The agent reads .agents/domain.md and finds Conventions: declined
The agent does not ask the user whether to create documentation/conventions.md
The agent returns to the caller and says the conventions step was skipped because it was declined earlier
No documentation/conventions.md is created

evals.prompt: Use the codify skill. Create a documentation/conventions.md for this project. A previous run recorded Conventions: declined in .agents/domain.md.
evals.expected_output: The direct request overrides the recorded decline and goes to the interview without an offer.
expectations: The agent does not ask whether to create documentation/conventions.md, since the user asked for it
The agent starts the code-convention interview through the interview skill, each question with a recommended answer
A previous decline does not stop the request

evals.prompt: Rename the `findOrder` function in evals/files/shop/src/orders.ts to `getOrder` and update its callers.
evals.expected_output: A plain rename; no conventions are drafted or offered.
expectations: The codify skill is not invoked
No conventions file is created or offered
